profile.summary: VenusREM predicts how single or multiple amino acid substitutions change a protein's fitness, without being trained on any measurements of the protein in question. It takes three inputs for the wild-type protein: its amino acid sequence, a structure in PDB format, and a set of homologous sequences found by alignment. A pretrained language model turns the sequence and the local structure around each residue into per-residue logits, a separate module turns the alignment into evolutionary logits, and the two are combined into one fitness score per mutant. The authors report Spearman correlations on 217 assays of the ProteinGym substitution benchmark and also test the model on a VHH antibody and on phi29 DNA polymerase mutants made in the laboratory.
profile.summary_source_locator: paper: Abstract, Section 2.1 Model overview, Section 2.4.3.1; README: Zero-shot Prediction for Mutants

summary_quotes.text: We present <sc>Venus</sc>REM, a retrieval-enhanced protein language model designed to capture local amino acid interactions in both spatial and temporal scales.
REM receives three sets of inputs: sequence, structure, and homolog information
This subset encompasses 217 high-throughput assays, totaling more than 2.5 million mutations.

we conducted a low-throughput post hoc analysis on more than 30 mutants to verify the model’s ability to improve the stability and binding affinity of a VHH antibody. We also validated the effectiveness of <sc>Venus</sc>REM by designing 10 novel mutants of a DNA polymerase and performing wet-lab experiments

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The sequence and the structure of the wild-type protein are first turned into tokens. The sequence uses a vocabulary of the 20 standard amino acids plus five special characters. For each residue the local structure, defined as up to 40 neighbouring residues within 10 angstroms, is embedded by a pretrained geometric vector perceptron trained as a denoising autoencoder on 4,735,677 local-structure graphs from CATH43-S40, and the resulting 256-dimensional vector is mapped by K-means into a codebook of 2048 structure tokens. A BERT-style protein language model combines the two token streams through disentangled multihead cross-attention to produce native logits for each residue and amino acid type. In parallel, homologous sequences retrieved by alignment are converted into evolutionary logits by a module that needs no extra training. A mutant's fitness score compares the logits of the mutant residues with those of the wild type, mixing the native and evolutionary terms; the mixing weight is the script's alpha option, which defaults to 0.8.

quotes.text: We construct a vocabulary for 20 standard AAs and 5 special characters
For each residue, we define its local structure by considering up to 40 neighboring residues within a 10 Å spatial radius.
We train a six-layer GVP with 4, 735, 677 graphs of local structures from <bold>CATH43-S40</bold>
These 256-dimensional vectors in the continuous space are further mapped to a 2048-dimensional discrete space using K-means clustering

The native representation, i.e. the joint embeddings of protein sequences and structures, are obtained by a BERT-style PLM. The core propagation rule is based on disentangled multihead cross-attention

The evolutionary representations are determined by an alignment tokenization module without additional training workload and are integrated into the fitness evaluation of mutants in a plug-and-play fashion.
For a given mutant, its fitness score is calculated by comparing the predicted logits of the mutant residues with those of the wild-type residues.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: VenusREM is a scoring pipeline rather than a single downloadable checkpoint. The pretrained weights it loads are frozen and live in a separate Hugging Face repository, AI4Protein/ProSST-2048, which the inference script loads by default; a result should name that revision as well as the commit of this repository. The repository's news list records later work under the same name: VenusREM2 reported at 0.556 on the ProteinGym substitution leaderboard through a separate VenusREM-Harness repository in September 2026, and an integration into VenusFactory2 in April 2026. Neither is described here as a checkpoint of its own. The score also depends on which homology search produced the alignment, since the repository offers prepared EVcouplings a2m files and ColabFold a3m files for ProteinGym and a Jackhmmer route for new proteins.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The language model was pretrained on sequences and structures from a Foldseek clustering of the AlphaFold2 database. The local structure autoencoder was trained on 4,735,677 local-structure graphs from CATH43-S40. No model weights are trained on deep mutational scanning data. The default retrieval method (EVcouplings) and the retrieval ratio of 0.8 were chosen on a validation subset made of 10% random samples from each of the 217 ProteinGym assays.

quotes.text: The training set for the pretrained language model is from Foldseek, which clusters the AlphaFold2 database to retain the original PDB structures and AA sequences.
We train a six-layer GVP with 4, 735, 677 graphs of local structures from <bold>CATH43-S40</bold>
The validation scores were assessed on a subset of ProteinGym with 10% random samples from each of the 217 assays.
we set the default retrieval method for <sc>Venus</sc>REM to <monospace>EVcouplings</monospace> with a 0.8 retrieval ratio.

strengths.text: The homology part is added at scoring time and needs no training, so a new alignment can be swapped in without refitting anything.

quotes.text: The evolutionary representations are determined by an alignment tokenization module without additional training workload and are integrated into the fitness evaluation of mutants in a plug-and-play fashion.

strengths.text: Inference does not need a forward pass per mutated position: the authors say their input preparation avoids mutating each position according to the DMS data or applying mask operations.

quotes.text: our method does not rely on mutating each position according to the DMS data (<xref rid="btaf189-B23" ref-type="bibr">Notin <italic toggle="yes">et al.</italic> 2022a</xref>) or applying mask operations

strengths.text: The hardware bar for inference is low by the authors' own account: they recommend at least 10 GB of graphics memory, such as an RTX 3080, and they ran the work on four of those cards.

quotes.text: For direct use of inference, we recommend at least 10G of graphics memory, such as RTX 3080
The model training and inference are performed on four NVIDIA 3080 GPUs with 10GB VRAM, using <monospace>PyTorch</monospace> version 2.4.1.

strengths.text: The authors tested the predictions outside high-throughput benchmarks, on 31 VHH antibody mutants from the literature and on ten phi29 DNA polymerase mutants they made and measured.

quotes.text: We extracted the experimental data of 31 VHH antibody mutants
Single-point saturation mutations were scored, and the top 10 mutants with the highest scores were selected for experimental validation.

diagram.caption: The pipeline of Figure 1 of the paper: sequence, structure and homologues are encoded separately, and the two sets of logits are mixed into one fitness score for each mutant.
diagram.source_locator: paper: Figure 1 caption and Section 2.3.3; compute_fitness.py: argument definitions

quotes.text: (a) For a given template protein, <sc>Venus</sc>REM encodes structural, sequence, and MSA information to generate logits for each residue, which are used to calculate mutation fitness scores. (b) For each AA, its local structure is clustered into 2048 distinct structure tokens. (c) The vector representations of structural and sequence information are integrated using disentangled cross-attention through BERT-style pretraining. (d) Homologous information is retrieved via <monospace>Jackhmmer</monospace> and converted to a matrix representation of evolutionary logits.

The benchmark numbers in the repository's results images were not read, because they are images.

run_guide.summary: Build the conda environment from the repository, fetch the prepared ProteinGym sequences, alignments and structures, and score the substitution assays with the default settings.
prerequisites: Anaconda3 or Miniconda3, as the README requires.
Python 3.9.20, the version pinned in environment.yml.
A GPU with at least 10 GB of graphics memory for inference, as the README recommends.
For new proteins rather than the prepared ProteinGym data: HMMER, EVcouplings and plmc, a UniRef100 download, a PDB structure, and eight CPU cores for the homology search.
The code is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so check the terms before any commercial or modified use.

limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.

The step for a protein of your own is longer: an alignment must be built with EVcouplings and selected with src/data/select_msa.py, a PDB structure obtained elsewhere, and structure sequences generated with src/data/get_struc_seq.py.
The archives other than aa_seq_aln_a2m.tar.gz are unpacked from the repository's own data folder, so the order of the commands matters.

notes: The paper gives the official repository as github.com/tyang816/VenusREM; the files here were fetched from ai4protein/VenusREM, whose README carries the same paper title and citation. No saved file states that one address redirects to the other. There is no Hugging Face model repository named AI4Protein/VenusREM (a request for its API record was refused); AI4Protein/VenusREM is a dataset repository holding the prepared ProteinGym inputs. All parameter and licence statements about the weights refer to AI4Protein/ProSST-2048, the frozen language model the script loads. VenusREM2 and its arXiv technical report were not fetched.
